title: Forests in the Salt Water
context:
Mangrove forests grow along tropical and subtropical coasts, in places where salt water would kill most trees. Around eighty tree species have evolved to tolerate these conditions, and together they cover about 150,000 square kilometres worldwide, an area roughly equal to that of Bangladesh. Indonesia alone holds the largest single share of the total, although mangroves are found on every continent that has a warm coastline. The forests vary greatly in appearance. In sheltered river deltas the trees can grow to more than thirty metres, forming a closed canopy, while on exposed or very salty shores they may be little more than dense shrubs no taller than a person. Local conditions of salt, tide and sediment decide which of the two forms develops.

Mangroves have developed a range of strategies for coping with their environment. Some species excrete salt through their leaves, while others prevent most of it from entering at the roots. Because the mud in which they grow is waterlogged and contains almost no oxygen, many trees send up specialised roots that rise above the surface and take in air directly. Reproduction is equally unusual. In several species the seed begins to germinate while still attached to the parent tree; the young plant then drops into the water and floats until it lodges in mud, where it can root quickly.

The tangled roots create a sheltered nursery. Juvenile fish, crabs and prawns hide among them from larger predators, and many commercially important species spend only part of their lives in mangroves before moving to open water or reefs. Coastal communities have long gathered wood, honey and shellfish from these forests, and in some regions fishing families say that catches fall noticeably when nearby mangroves are cleared.

Mangroves also protect the land behind them. Their dense roots and trunks slow waves and reduce erosion. After the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, some studies suggested that villages sheltered by mangroves suffered fewer casualties, but other researchers have cautioned that the effect depends on the width of the forest belt and the size of the wave, and that no mangrove forest can stop a very large tsunami. A further benefit is climate related. Mangrove soils accumulate dead plant material that decays slowly in the absence of oxygen, so a hectare of mangrove locks away several times as much carbon as a hectare of most tropical forests, much of it below ground.

Despite these benefits, roughly one fifth of the world's mangroves have been lost since 1980. The main cause has been conversion to shrimp ponds, followed by agriculture and urban development. Efforts at restoration have had mixed results. Many planting schemes fail because seedlings are placed on mudflats where mangroves never grew naturally, or because the flow of tidal water that the trees need has been blocked. Projects that first restore the tides and then allow natural regrowth tend to do better. Some governments now pay coastal communities to guard remaining forests, although enforcement remains uneven.

questions.prompt: Mangroves are able to grow where salt water would be fatal to most other trees.
questions.why: Câu đầu nói chúng mọc ở nơi nước mặn giết hầu hết cây.
questions.quote: in places where salt water would kill most trees

questions.prompt: The total area of the world's mangrove forests is greater than the area of Bangladesh.
questions.why: Diện tích 'roughly equal' Bangladesh, không lớn hơn.
questions.quote: an area roughly equal to that of Bangladesh

questions.prompt: Brazil has the second largest area of mangrove forest in the world.
questions.why: Bài chỉ nêu Indonesia có phần lớn nhất, không nói về Brazil.

questions.prompt: Certain mangrove species get rid of salt through their leaves.
questions.why: Một số loài thải muối qua lá.
questions.quote: Some species excrete salt through their leaves

questions.prompt: All mangrove species prevent salt from entering through their roots.
questions.why: Chỉ 'others' chặn muối ở rễ; một số loài thải qua lá.
questions.quote: others prevent most of it from entering at the roots

questions.prompt: Some mangroves have roots that rise above the mud to take in air.
questions.why: Rễ chuyên hoá nhô lên khỏi mặt bùn để hút không khí.
questions.quote: send up specialised roots that rise above the surface and take in air directly

questions.prompt: Mangrove roots rise above the mud because the soil is too salty for them.
questions.why: Lý do là bùn ngập nước và thiếu oxy, không phải quá mặn.
questions.quote: the mud in which they grow is waterlogged and contains almost no oxygen

questions.prompt: In some species, seeds start to develop before leaving the parent tree.
questions.why: Hạt bắt đầu nảy mầm khi còn gắn trên cây mẹ.
questions.quote: the seed begins to germinate while still attached to the parent tree

questions.prompt: Mangrove seedlings can drift for hundreds of kilometres before taking root.
questions.why: Bài chỉ nói chúng trôi cho tới khi mắc vào bùn, không nêu khoảng cách.

questions.prompt: Young fish choose to shelter in mangrove roots rather than in coral reefs.
questions.why: Bài không so sánh sự ưa thích giữa rễ đước và rạn san hô.

questions.prompt: Every commercially important fish species stays in mangroves for its whole life.
questions.why: Nhiều loài chỉ sống ở đó một phần đời rồi ra biển khơi hoặc rạn.
questions.quote: spend only part of their lives in mangroves

questions.prompt: Fishing families have said that clearing mangroves can reduce their catches.
questions.why: Bài ghi nhận các gia đình ngư dân nói sản lượng giảm khi rừng bị phá.
questions.quote: catches fall noticeably when nearby mangroves are cleared

questions.prompt: Mangrove forests reduce the height of incoming waves by more than half.
questions.why: Bài chỉ nói rễ làm chậm sóng, không đưa tỉ lệ giảm cụ thể.

questions.prompt: All researchers agree that mangroves saved lives during the 2004 tsunami.
questions.why: Chỉ 'some studies suggested'; các nhà nghiên cứu khác thận trọng về hiệu quả.
questions.quote: other researchers have cautioned that the effect depends on the width of the forest belt

questions.prompt: Mangrove forests are unable to stop a very large tsunami.
questions.why: Không rừng đước nào chặn được sóng thần rất lớn.
questions.quote: no mangrove forest can stop a very large tsunami

questions.prompt: A large amount of the carbon held by mangroves is found underground.
questions.why: Phần lớn carbon nằm 'below ground'.

questions.prompt: Satellite measurements have shown that mangroves store more carbon than any other ecosystem.
questions.why: Bài không nhắc vệ tinh hay so sánh với mọi hệ sinh thái.

questions.prompt: About half of the world's mangroves have disappeared since 1980.
questions.why: Bài nói khoảng một phần năm, không phải một nửa.
questions.quote: roughly one fifth of the world's mangroves have been lost since 1980

questions.prompt: Shrimp farming has been the leading reason for mangrove loss.
questions.why: Nguyên nhân chính là chuyển thành ao nuôi tôm.
questions.quote: The main cause has been conversion to shrimp ponds

questions.prompt: Mangrove planting schemes are successful wherever they are carried out.
questions.why: Nhiều dự án thất bại do trồng sai chỗ hoặc thiếu dòng triều.
